facts.claim: Traditionally, men do not go to bridal showers, but modern etiquette says the couple decides. Co-ed showers, often called Jack and Jill showers, are increasingly common. Invite the men who matter to you both, or keep it women only. Both are correct.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers?
facts.use_note: Own page (published 2016-04, modified 2026-07-20). Sibling owns the men/co-ed question; link to it with a non-exact anchor and do not repeat its debate.

facts.claim: The guiding rule is simple: everyone on the shower guest list should also be invited to the wedding, and the host, often the maid of honor or a member of the wedding party, sets the tone.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers?
facts.use_note: Core house rule. Present as our convention, not law. Page uses US spelling 'maid of honor'; use 'maid of honour' in our AU copy. Destination nuance (small guest list abroad) must stay consistent with this rule; see F-03 and gaps.

facts.claim: Does everyone invited to the bridal shower have to be invited to the wedding? Yes. It is the one firm rule of shower etiquette. Everyone on the shower guest list should also be on the wedding guest list.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers? (FAQ)
facts.use_note: FAQ wording. Our new article must not contradict this 'one firm rule'. Any exception (e.g. office showers, destination micro weddings) needs Nic/editor decision; logged in needs.

facts.claim: Who usually attends a bridal shower? Traditionally the women closest to the bride, hosted by the maid of honor or a member of the wedding party, who sets the tone. Modern etiquette leaves the guest list open, including co-ed formats.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers? (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Convention, present as advice.

facts.claim: A co-ed shower that welcomes partners and close male friends is often called a Jack and Jill. It works especially well when the couple already shares one social circle.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers? (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Mention briefly, link to sibling.

facts.claim: Fiona Deans-Dundas (Couture Wedding Planning): 'If the bride does have a close male friend or brother that may feel left when not invited, I would suggest that the bride arrange a separate lunch or dinner date, so that they feel more involved.'
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers?
facts.use_note: Named expert quote on our page, originally 2016. Usable as attributed opinion if needed; quote verbatim with attribution.

facts.claim: Wendy Daoud El-Khoury (Wedded Wonderland): 'Once upon a time, I had a bridal shower, and many of my friends missed out. Not because I wanted them to, but because they weren't invited. Why? Because apparently the Bridal Showers and Kitchen Teas are not for boys. Well not anymore!'
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers?
facts.use_note: Founder voice; first-person brand quote. Shows the brand uses 'bridal shower' and 'kitchen tea' interchangeably (Australian term).

facts.claim: Sibling page SEO: title 'Are Men Invited to Bridal Showers? Etiquette Guide'; meta 'Are men invited to bridal showers? Modern bridal shower etiquette on guest lists, co-ed showers and who to include - answered clearly.'; tags 'Advice|bridal shower'.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland page metadata
facts.use_note: Cannibalisation: sibling meta already mentions 'guest lists' and 'who to include'. Partial overlap. Ours must own the full list (tiers, numbers, destination, virtual) and send men/co-ed to the sibling. Its CTA links /wonderland-concierge ('Wedded Concierge').

facts.claim: Guests are usually the bridal party, close family and friends of the bride who are also invited to the wedding. The bride gives the host her guest list, and the host sends the invitations. Leave off anyone who isn't invited to the wedding, since a shower invitation implies a wedding one.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Host Etiquette Explained (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Own page, consistent with F-02/F-03. Use for 'who decides' and 'core invite list'.

facts.claim: Family hosts tend to have a say in the guest list and the setting, especially when they are paying.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Host Etiquette Explained
facts.use_note: Useful for the paying_parent persona. Present as advice.

facts.claim: A bride who lives far from her family may have two showers: one with friends near her home, and one with relatives in her home town.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Host Etiquette Explained
facts.use_note: Supports a 'more than one shower' section. Guest-overlap etiquette between two showers is not covered on our pages; see needs.

facts.claim: It can [be a surprise], but the bride should still provide the guest list, so the right people are there.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Host Etiquette Explained
facts.use_note: Surprise showers: guest list still from the bride.

facts.claim: Many showers now include guests of every gender and are called wedding showers or couple's showers.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Host Etiquette Explained
facts.use_note: Terminology. Sibling page (F-05) uses 'Jack and Jill'; both are on our pages.

facts.claim: Most showers are held between a few weeks and four months before the wedding. Pick a date when the bride and most guests are free, and avoid the final fortnight.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Host Etiquette Explained (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Timing window. The destination page attributes the same window to Vogue, so this convention ultimately rests on a publisher; present as advice in our voice, do not cite Vogue.

facts.claim: You don't need one, but it is worth hosting when many people close to the bride can't travel to the wedding. A shower at home lets them share in the lead-up without a flight, a hotel and time off work.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, How to Host a Destination Bridal Shower
facts.use_note: Key destination-edge fact: shower at home for those who cannot travel.

facts.claim: Who should be invited to a destination bridal shower? Anyone invited to the wedding can come, including the guests who can't make the trip. Leave off people who aren't invited to the wedding: a shower invitation implies a wedding one, and it comes with the expectation of a gift. The bridal party and immediate family usually head the list.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, How to Host a Destination Bridal Shower (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Answers 'inviting people who cannot travel'. Same page also says 'Vogue's guide to bridal showers lists the bridal party, close family and friends attending the wedding as the usual guests'; do not repeat the Vogue attribution, use our own FAQ wording.

facts.claim: If most of the bride's friends are travelling for the wedding, you can hold the shower there. A brunch or afternoon tea at the resort early in the wedding week is the simplest option. Keep it optional and close to where everyone is staying, since guests are paying for flights and accommodation too. Schedule it on a different day from the welcome party, or fold the two together if the guest lists match.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, How to Host a Destination Bridal Shower
facts.use_note: Shower at home vs near the wedding. Link /expert-advice/do-you-need-a-wedding-welcome-party.

facts.claim: Send the invitations four to six weeks ahead. Include the date, time, place, dress code and registry details.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, How to Host a Destination Bridal Shower
facts.use_note: Our page attributes the 4 to 6 week notice to Vogue. Planning page (F-19) states the same in our own voice; cite that one.

facts.claim: Send the invitations. Post them four to six weeks before the shower, with the when and where, what to wear and where the couple is registered.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Planning Guide From Invites to Games
facts.use_note: Own voice, no third-party attribution. Preferred source for invitation timing. Note its checklist item 08 says 'a month to six weeks out' (minor internal wording variance).

facts.claim: Draw up the guest list. The bride or her family should supply it, and everyone on it should have a wedding invitation too.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Planning Guide From Invites to Games
facts.use_note: Guest list step sits in the 'three months before' block, alongside host, date and budget. Planning page owns the timeline; our article should link to it, not repeat the timeline.

facts.claim: Confirm numbers with the venue or caterer. Chase any guests who haven't replied.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Planning Guide From Invites to Games
facts.use_note: RSVP follow-up, one week before.

facts.claim: Shower timing before the wedding: the planning page says 'Most showers fall one to three months before the wedding'; the host etiquette and destination pages say 'Most showers are held between a few weeks and four months before the wedding'.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Planning Guide; also /celebration-ideas/who-hosts-bridal-shower
facts.use_note: CONFLICT between our own pages. If timing is mentioned, say 'one to three months' (fits inside both ranges) or avoid a figure. Flag to editor to align the two pages.

facts.claim: A winery, garden or spa day suits a smaller group that wants an experience as much as a party.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Planning Guide From Invites to Games
facts.use_note: Links guest-list size to venue choice. No page of ours gives a typical shower guest count; see needs.

facts.claim: If the wedding is overseas, hold the shower at home well before the bride flies out, and steer guests towards gifts that are delivered rather than carried.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Bridal Shower Planning Guide From Invites to Games
facts.use_note: Destination edge; link /celebration-ideas/destination-bridal-shower.

facts.claim: Wonderland Studio: 'Guest list and RSVPs, budget, seating, your wedding website and seven more tools, guided by luxury wedding experts.' 'Free to use · no credit card · no trial clock'.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wonderland Studio
facts.use_note: Brand fact. brand-profile.md words it 'Free to use, no credit card required.' Either wording is approved; quote one exactly. Page date not shown; source_date is the check month.

facts.claim: Every RSVP, the moment it lands: 'Replies, plus-ones and dietary notes arrive straight into your guest list.' RSVPs with the details that matter: 'Guests tell you who is coming and what they eat, in one tap.'
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wonderland Studio
facts.use_note: Guest list and RSVP tool feature wording. Page shows RSVP options Going, Not going, Maybe.

facts.claim: Wonderland Studio is a free celebration planning suite. You get an event website with RSVP, a guest list, budget, timeline, seating, menu and vendor tools, trusted vendor recommendations and an AI Planning Assistant. Wonderland Studio is for anyone planning a milestone worth doing properly - a destination wedding, an engagement party, a honeymoon, a landmark anniversary or birthday.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wonderland Studio (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Supports suggesting Studio for keeping the wedding and shower lists in one place, but the page does not name bridal showers specifically. Do not claim a 'shower guest list' feature; say the guest list and RSVP tools are free to use. Source contains a hyphen used as a dash; paraphrase rather than quoting that part to keep copy free of dashes.

facts.claim: Free accounts can hold a generous guest list. Share your account with your partner, and if you work with a wedding planner who uses Wedded Wonderland, they can plan alongside you inside Wonderland Studio.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wonderland Studio (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Account sharing. Page does not say a maid of honour or shower host can be given access; do not claim it.

facts.claim: Anyone invited to your engagement party, bridal shower, or hens or bucks celebration should also be invited to the wedding. An invitation to one celebration naturally signals an invitation to the next. If your wedding will be small, keep those earlier guest lists small too.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette: Who Do You Have to Invite?
facts.use_note: Strongest own-page wording for the core rule, plus the 'keep earlier lists small' advice for small or destination weddings. Cluster page; link with a guest-list-etiquette anchor.

facts.claim: A destination wedding guest list is usually smaller, gathered closely around the inner circle, because an invitation asks guests to give their time, their leave and their travel. A small, faraway wedding also softens the engagement party rule, provided guests understand the celebration is intimate by design.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette: Who Do You Have to Invite?
facts.use_note: CONFLICT with F-03 ('the one firm rule of shower etiquette'). This page softens the pre-wedding-party rule for small faraway weddings (named for engagement parties only, not showers). Do not extend the softening to showers without an editor decision; see N-01.

facts.claim: Etiquette expects you to invite immediate family, your wedding party, the partners of married or cohabiting guests, and anyone already invited to a pre-wedding celebration. Every other name is a choice.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette: Who Do You Have to Invite?
facts.use_note: Context for building a shower list down from the wedding list.

facts.claim: Colleagues belong on your wedding guest list only if you share a friendship outside work. If most of your team is coming, include your manager as well.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette: Who Do You Have to Invite?
facts.use_note: Wedding-list advice only. Our pages say nothing about office or workplace showers specifically; see N-02.

facts.claim: The guest list manager in Wonderland Studio lets you group these names by category from your very first draft. With your list kept in Wonderland Studio, every decision sits in one place for both families.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette: Who Do You Have to Invite?
facts.use_note: Own wording for Studio's grouping by category. Supports a line like 'tag shower guests within your wedding list' only if phrased as grouping by category; no dedicated shower feature is stated.

facts.claim: Why do some guests decline a destination wedding? Travel, leave and family commitments mean a destination wedding often receives more declines than a local one. Respond warmly without asking for a reason, and keep those guests in mind for a gathering at home after the wedding.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette (FAQ)
facts.use_note: Pairs with F-15/F-16: guests who cannot travel can still be on the shower list.

facts.claim: Parents who contribute financially often expect a voice in the guest list. Agree early on a set number of places for each side of the family, and let them choose within it.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland, Wedding Guest List Etiquette: Who Do You Have to Invite?
facts.use_note: Wedding-list advice; pairs with F-10 for the paying_parent persona. Apply to showers only as advice.

facts.claim: Wonderland Studio in brand profile: 'Free planning suite: website and RSVPs, guest list and seating, budget (multi-currency), timeline, vendor shortlists, AI planning assistant. "Free to use, no credit card required."' URL /wonderland-studio.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland brand profile

needs.what: Editor decision: is 'every shower guest is invited to the wedding' absolute (F-03 says 'the one firm rule'), or does the small faraway wedding softening (F-30, stated for engagement parties) extend to showers? Article must pick one and stay consistent with both pages.
Office or workplace showers thrown by colleagues who are not invited to the wedding: no own-page position. Present as advice or omit.
Typical bridal shower guest count or size range: not on any of our pages. Present as advice without numbers, or supply from planning team experience.
Virtual or video-call guests at a shower (for guests overseas): not on any of our pages. Present as advice.
Two showers (F-11): etiquette for guest overlap and gifts between showers is not on our pages. Present as advice.
Shower timing conflict between our pages (F-22): align 'one to three months' vs 'a few weeks to four months'.
Whether Wonderland Studio's guest list can hold a separate shower list or event (events, tags, multiple RSVP forms). Live page does not say. Confirm with product before claiming.
A real client story of a shower before a destination wedding (with consent), if wanted.

Conventions not on our pages and to be framed as advice only: inviting the groom's family, mothers and grandmothers by default, children at showers, plus-ones at showers, inviting people who declined the wedding, sending gifts when not attending.
